free_tier.stated: District government guideline, verbatim: 'The laboratory construction period is no more than 3 years; first-year support is no more than CNY 27,000,000, spent on compute rental, related configuration and operations. The laboratory compute serves no fewer than 30 quality projects or talent teams each year and must convert at least 8 into companies.' Eligibility, verbatim: 'The project founder or individual must meet at least one of: 1. a QS top-200 university background; 2. work experience at a leading domestic or overseas big-tech firm; 3. work experience at a star startup valued above CNY 1 billion or an AI unicorn; 4. fine-tuning experience on 8 or more GPUs; 5. an existing product demo plus open-source contribution, such as a GitHub or Hugging Face project with at least 100 stars; 6. backing from multiple investors.'

chaining: This is the upstream reason the MiraclePlus ceiling exists. The credits a researcher receives are municipal money administered by an operator, so the award size is bounded by a district budget line rather than by a commercial free tier. It composes with nothing, because it is the funding behind the resource and not a resource itself.

notes: THE NUMBER THAT DECIDES THE SHAPE: CNY 27,000,000 divided by at least 30 projects gives an average ceiling near CNY 900,000 per project, consistent with and slightly below the published CNY 1,000,000 maximum. That is arithmetic proof that the million is a per-project cap inside a fixed municipal budget, not a standard award. TWO LAYERS, and the distinction carries the verdict: the laboratory guideline is a credential screen written for the operating entity and its intake; MiraclePlus runs its own intake in front of it and publishes no such list, naming instead research capability, technical fit and project potential. An unaffiliated individual therefore faces no formal document barrier but a de facto one, because the intake behind the panel selects for exactly those credentials. The fails-identity verdict is recorded against this record because the public funding terms are the ones that bind; the sibling MiraclePlus record carries the softer verdict so a reader sees both. UNCERTAIN: whether MiraclePlus applies the six criteria literally to every compute applicant or uses them only as a preference.
